::: {.content-visible when-profile="instructor"}
::: {.callout-important title="Instructor-only guide to Part II (not on the student site)"}
Model milestones and verified numbers for the amniote investigation. The
served file now ships the archive's raw values, sentinel codes included;
nothing on the student page discloses this. The discovery is the point.

**Stage 1 (structure).** Shape 21,322 x 10. A naive audit reads every
column as 100% complete: there are zero true NaNs in the served file.
Full credit requires noticing this is too good to be true (or discovering
it at stage 3 and revising).

**Stage 2 (unit of analysis).** Classes: Aves 9,802, Reptilia 6,567,
Mammalia 4,953 (sums to 21,322). 465 families; largest is Scincidae
(skinks, 1,351 species), then Gekkonidae (701); 67 families contain a
single species.

**Stage 3 (validation), the planted discovery chain.** The archive codes
missing values as **-999**. Counts per trait column: mass 4,645;
longevity 15,822; litter/clutch 8,244; maturity 17,849; birth weight
17,779. Any physical rule fires at these ("mass <= 0" catches 4,645
rows), and any log transform crashes; the Stage 3 hint ("a rule that
fires far more often than errors plausibly occur has found a convention")
points here without naming it. After students recode -999 to NA, the real
missingness appears (22% to 84% by column: most of the table) and two
second-layer defects remain: **4 rows with maturity <= 0 days** and **35
rows where maturity exceeds longevity** once maturity is converted from
days to years (of 3,126 rows with both observed). The unit trap is
deliberate. External species checks against a handbook pass comfortably.

**Stages 4 and 5 (the classic pair).** After recoding: mass vs longevity
gives 5,122 species (24%); species-level r of the logged traits 0.519;
family means of logged values (group by class and family, reset_index)
give **327 families, r = 0.649**. The raw grams trap: the mean of logs is
the log of the geometric mean, the right average for ratio-scale traits;
averaging unlogged mass lets single giants drag family means.

**Marking guide.** Full credit needs: stated expectations with sources;
discovery and explicit handling of the sentinel convention (recode, drop,
or mask, any is fine if disclosed); at least one second-layer defect
found with counts; an explicit row-flow for the chosen pair; and a final
caption naming unit, n, transformations, scales, and drops. Reward
students who choose a pair other than mass-longevity and reason about its
much smaller complete-case sample. Students who report "no missing data"
at stage 1 and never revisit have missed the core lesson.
